title: Optimizing Risk-Adapted Lipid Therapy in Post-Stroke Patients: A prospective registry study in University and Rural Hospital Settings – Lipid-Stroke-Registry
summary:
fter ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, consistent lowering of LDL cholesterol is an important part of preventing further vascular events. Although clear recommendations for LDL-C targets exist, these targets are often not achieved in routine clinical care. A key question is whether patients receive lipid-lowering therapy early after stroke that is adapted to their individual vascular risk and whether necessary treatment adjustments are implemented during follow-up.

The Lipid-Stroke-Registry investigates real-world lipid management after stroke or TIA across different hospital settings. At Jena University Hospital, a structured Lipid Visit is performed as part of routine clinical care. This includes documentation of LDL-C levels, prior lipid-lowering therapy, vascular risk, target orientation and planned further treatment. The study does not mandate any specific medication; all treatment decisions remain part of standard medical care.

Patients treated at Jena University Hospital with a Lipid Visit are compared with a historical UKJ cohort from the period before implementation of the Lipid Visit and with patients from other hospitals within the SATELIT network. The aim is to assess, under real-world conditions, how often LDL-C targets are achieved, which treatment patterns are used and where lipid secondary prevention after stroke can be further improved.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Baseline LDL-C measurement available before initiation of lipid-lowering therapy
Exclusion criteria:
Intracerebral hemorrhage or primary hemorrhagic stroke
• Premorbid life expectancy < 5 months (e.g. advanced malignancy, end-stage organ failure)
• Known intolerance or contraindication to all study lipid-lowering agents (rosuvastatin, atorvastatin, ezetimibe, bempedoic acid)
• Severe hepatic impairment (ALT/AST > 3 × upper limit of normal, urea upper limit) or decompensated liver disease
• End-stage renal disease requiring dialysis
• Pregnancy or breastfeeding
